successors.note: Tripartite Convention signed at Washington 2 December 1899, ratifications exchanged 16 February 1900.

successors.note: Manuʻa's deeds of cession were only signed in 1904 (6 July 1904, Tui Manuʻa Elisala).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Samoa row before the modern country). The infobox gives no area; the successors are German Samoa and American Samoa. The partition line the 1899 convention drew (171 degrees W) is the western island group for Germany; the page does not say Tutuila's chiefs were under the Malo, so Tutuila is a confidence-2 inclusion, and Manuʻa (a separate kingdom that 'joined American Samoa in 1904') is excluded.

region.text: Upolu, Savaii, Apolima and Manono (Samoa) and Tutuila with Aunuu (American Samoa); the Manuʻa Islands, a separate chiefdom until 1904, are not drawn

ledger.note: 1873: the Kingdom of Samoa is founded with Tupua Pulepule and Malietoa Laupepa as kings. Infobox 'Capital: Mulinuʻu (1873-1887 ...)' and rulers 'Tupua Pulepule and Malietoa Laupepa 1873-1875'; the lead says the monarchy was founded in 1873. The predecessor on the page is the Faitasiga (confederacy). The land is the researcher's reading of the page's 'Polynesian monarchy on the Samoan Islands' and its two successors.
1880: the government is at Leulumoega (infobox 'Leulumoega (1880-1881, 1887-1888)'); the infobox spans overlap Mulinuʻu's 1873-1887 and are resolved here by the narrower span.
1889: back at Mulinuʻu after Tamasese's years at Leulumoega (infobox 'Mulinuʻu (1873-1887, 1889-1899)').

region.text: Upolu, Savaii, Apolima and Manono (Samoa) and Tutuila with Aunuu (American Samoa); the Manuʻa Islands, a separate chiefdom until 1904, are not drawn

ledger.note: 1900: the Samoan monarchy ends and the islands are partitioned. 'The monarchy was abolished under the Tripartite Convention of 1899, effective 16 February 1900' (Kingdom of Samoa page); signed at Washington on 2 December 1899, ratified 16 February 1900; Upolu, Savaii, Apolima and Manono to Germany, Tutuila and the islands east of 171 degrees W to the US (order of 19 February 1900).

wars.name: War between Pulefou and Taimua and Faipule
wars.outcome: No ground recorded as changing hands; the Taimua and Faipule government sat at Leulumoega in 1880-1881 (infobox capitals).
wars.note: Infobox: 'War between Pulefou and Taimua and Faipule: 1879-1881'. An internal war of the kingdom between its factions; zones empty because the page names no ground that changed hands. Added by the reviewer (oc-01).

wars.name: First Samoan Civil War
wars.outcome: No territorial change: Samoan factions (Tamasese, Mataʻafa, Malietoa Laupepa) fought with German, British and American intervention; the warships of the three powers at Apia were wrecked by the storm of 15 March 1889.
wars.note: Body text 1886-1894, infobox 1889-1894. The 1889 Treaty of Berlin is not described on either page.

wars.name: Second Samoan Civil War

zones.text: Apia and Vailele, where Mataʻafa's rebels fought Tanu's forces and the British and American landing parties

wars.outcome: Battle of Apia in March 1899 (Apia shelled 15 March 1899); Mataʻafa's rebels defeated an allied force at Vailele on 1 April 1899; settled by the partition of 2 December 1899.
wars.note: No rebel state is drawn: the infobox names Aele as Mataʻafa's capital in 1899 but no page gives territory he held.

certainty.note: Island coasts are exact; the monarchy's real authority over Tutuila and the villages was contested by rival kings and the three powers.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (the Samoa row is the modern country from 1962). Not on any page opened: the pre-1873 districts and the tafaʻifa (A'ana, Atua, Tuamasaga, Aiga-i-le-Tai ...), the dates of the Tongan period in Samoa (the Tuʻi Manuʻa page: 'almost 400 years', expelled in the 13th century, matching the Tuʻi Tonga dossier), the 1879-1881 war of Pulefou against Taimua and Faipule (named only in the infobox), the Treaty of Berlin (1889), the Municipality of Apia, the extent of Mataʻafa's rebel government in 1899. Manuʻa (Tuʻi Manuʻa) needs its own dossier but no page opened dates its beginning or its boundaries, only the 6 July 1904 cession; counterparts_needing_dossiers. The kings list is the infobox's and overlaps in 1887-1893. Region names: 'Samoa' and 'American Samoa' are Natural Earth countries; the Manuʻa admin-1 resolves to no land cells at the grid's resolution. Capital coordinates approximate.
